negative_findings.why_it_matters: The official portal is the upstream of every source in this cell; its availability pattern determines whether the open-data layer must be the primary collection route.

negative_findings.description: OtvorenéZmluvy.sk current operational status could not be confirmed. Search results describe the portal and its ~300k contracts and a GitHub organisation exists, but no direct fetch was performed and no recent (2024-2026) evidence of active updating was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Recorded as a candidate with low confidence and access_status 'unverified' rather than as live or dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If dormant, its red-flag scoring layer would need to be reimplemented over CRZ rather than consumed; if live, it saves substantial work.

negative_findings.description: No Slovak open-data or civil-society product was found that is specific to banking, payments or financial-sector procurement. All discovered analytics layers are sector-agnostic and must be filtered by CPV code, buyer identity or supplier identity to isolate banking/payments relevance.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searched sk and en for procurement-analytics tooling; every hit is a general-purpose corpus or aggregator.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sector isolation is our own work, not something the ecosystem provides. Requires an explicit CPV shortlist (financial/insurance services, banking software, payment terminals, card personalisation, ATM/self-service, IT services) and a curated buyer list (NBS, Slovenská pošta, state banks and agencies) to be defined before collection.

negative_findings.description: Neither the Slovenská FinTech asociácia nor SAF exposed a scrapable, complete member list in search results; SBA's exact member roster page was also not directly surfaced (only the aggregate '23 members / >99% of the sector' statement on the About page).
negative_findings.result_summary: Association identities and URLs confirmed, but member rosters need direct on-site navigation or an email request to the secretariat (sekretariat@slovakfintech.sk).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor-side actor coverage for A2 stays incomplete until these rosters are captured; missing vendor names means missing tender award matches.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Slovak for a dedicated card/payments industry association (analogue of a national card association or ATM/POS operators' body) and found none; the space appears to be covered by SBA, the two fintech associations and ITAS.
negative_findings.result_summary: No Slovak card/payments-specific trade association identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: There is no single membership list that enumerates POS/ATM/acquiring vendors; that universe must be assembled from ITAS, fintech associations and tender award notices instead.

negative_findings.description: ORSR has no confirmed official public REST API; reporting points to a pilot Swagger at obcan.justice.sk and weekly SQL dumps at justice.gov.sk/sluzby/registre/otvorene-data. Neither was fetched or verified in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bulk access route for the commercial register is plausible but unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Actor-graph construction depends on IČO joins; if bulk access is unavailable, per-entity scraping raises cost and blocking risk.

negative_findings.description: The DORA 'register informácií' collects each financial entity's ICT third-party providers, but no evidence was found that NBS publishes entity-level contents.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the framework/guidance page appears public.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Would otherwise be the single best map of who supplies IT to Slovak banks; its likely confidentiality means vendor mapping must rely on tenders and association lists.

negative_findings.description: No Slovak trade outlet was found that systematically and specifically covers procurement of payment infrastructure by commercial banks (as opposed to state IT). Coverage of private-bank vendor selection is incidental and largely PR-driven.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in SK for bank core-system / payment-platform supplier contracts returned mostly procurement aggregators and general tech magazine items, not journalistic deal reporting.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Private-sector (sector=both) payment/banking deals in SK will have to be reconstructed from PR wires, vendor press rooms and international trade press rather than from local journalism.

negative_findings.description: The Slovak term 'tender' collides with the commercial aggregator brand tender.sk and with verejnesutaze.sk listings, which dominate SERPs and crowd out journalism.
negative_findings.result_summary: Three of five SK queries returned mostly tender.sk / verejnesutaze.sk / TED pages instead of media articles.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Media-cell collection must exclude aggregator domains or use site-scoped queries, otherwise recall on journalistic sources is very low.

negative_findings.description: The core business titles for this cell (Trend, Hospodárske noviny, Denník E, Forbes SK) are wholly or partly paywalled.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only headlines/ledes reliably reachable without subscription.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Full-text signal extraction (named suppliers, contract values) will require paid subscriptions or human review; automated collection alone will under-report.

negative_findings.description: No page in this slice was fetched directly; all URLs come from search-result metadata or prior domain knowledge. None is claimed as verified live.
negative_findings.result_summary: Discovery performed via search only; liveness left to the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Some section paths (e.g. itnews.sk, forbes.sk homepages) may redirect or have changed structure.

negative_findings.description: English-language reporting on Slovak banking/payments tenders is very thin; the Slovak Spectator and international fintech press cover it only sporadically.
negative_findings.result_summary: EN-oriented seed query returned no dedicated EN outlet for SK bank tender coverage.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: EN-only monitoring would miss nearly all of this cell's signal; SK-language collection is mandatory here.

negative_findings.description: No single consolidated, machine-readable 'pipeline of upcoming public IT tenders' register was found for Slovakia. The pipeline has to be reconstructed by joining MetaIS project records, MIRRI public-consultation notices and MF SR/ÚHP ex-ante appraisals.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches in Slovak for a consolidated list of prepared informatization projects returned only per-project consultation notices, not an aggregate register.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must be multi-source and join-based; a single-feed assumption would miss most pre-tender signals.

negative_findings.description: No public vendor-day / supplier-day agendas published by individual Slovak banks (SLSP, VÚB, Tatra banka, ČSOB, 365.bank) were located in either language.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches surfaced only career pages and general conferences; bank-hosted supplier events appear to be invitation-only and unpublished.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: One of the cell's hypothesised signal types (vendor days) is likely not observable via open web collection for commercial banks; the equivalent signal must be taken from third-party conferences and sponsor lists instead.

negative_findings.description: MetaIS project/ISVS detail pages were not fetched in this pass; the older host metais.vicepremier.gov.sk still appears in search indexes while the current portal is metais.slovensko.sk.
negative_findings.result_summary: Search results returned a legacy-host deep link; current-host reachability not tested here.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Legacy links should be treated as moved (redirect/rewrite to the current host) rather than dead; a deterministic verification pass should resolve both hosts.

negative_findings.description: LinkedIn job postings and LinkedIn company pages for Slovak banks and state agencies were not assessed as a collectable source in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only the SBA LinkedIn company page appeared incidentally in results; no assessment of LinkedIn job-feed accessibility was made.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: LinkedIn carries many senior payments/vendor-management roles that never reach profesia.sk, but it is login-walled and ToS-restricted, so its status needs an explicit decision.

negative_findings.description: Local-language terminology for 'vendor day' / 'supplier day' in a banking context has no established Slovak equivalent; searches used English-in-Slovak forms only.
negative_findings.result_summary: No productive sk term identified beyond 'dodávateľský deň' (not attested in results).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: This term family should be treated as untested rather than exhausted; future passes should try 'stretnutie s dodávateľmi', 'trhová konzultácia', 'prípravné trhové konzultácie' (the last is the legally defined pre-tender market consultation term).

negative_findings.description: No official REST API for CRZ was found. Community requests for a CRZ API exist on platforma.slovensko.digital (thread 'Centrálny register zmlúv API'), and the only official machine-readable channel found is the dated ZIP/XML change-batch export plus the HTML search UI.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bulk XML export exists; no documented official query API. Third-party APIs (Slovensko.Digital Datahub) fill the gap but are commercial.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must be crawl/bulk-parse based, with rate-limit compliance, not API-based; budget for parsing effort and for a possible paid aggregator dependency.

negative_findings.description: Slovak law removes exactly the contract types most relevant to this cell from full publication in some cases: sources describing §5a ods. 5 of Act 211/2000 state that for certain letters (incl. contracts on securities/financial instruments and contracts securing the provision of payment services) only information about the conclusion of the contract is published, not the contract text. Sources also state that since 31.3.2022 only NBS retains a full entity-level exemption.
negative_findings.result_summary: Payment-services and financial-instrument contracts may appear only as a bare notice of conclusion, without price or terms.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Absence of a full contract in CRZ is not evidence of no deal; analysis must treat these as censored observations and fall back to invoice registers, ÚVO notices and institutional pages.

negative_findings.description: https://data.gov.sk/dataset/crz returned HTTP 302 to https://data.slovensko.sk/datasety/crz; the target rendered as an empty JS shell to a plain fetch, so the resource list, licence and update frequency could not be read.
negative_findings.result_summary: Dataset almost certainly live at the new national catalogue domain, but its distributions were not confirmed by me.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The open-data catalogue migrated (data.gov.sk to data.slovensko.sk); any stored CRZ dataset URLs in the collection pipeline are likely stale and need re-resolution, and the page probably needs a JS-capable fetcher.

negative_findings.description: A targeted Slovak query combining 'spracovanie platobných kariet', 'platobný terminál' and 'POS terminál' against CRZ returned mostly generic CRZ landing/FAQ pages and bank T&C PDFs rather than contract hits, indicating the public web index does not reach deep into CRZ contract detail pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: General web search is a poor discovery channel for individual CRZ contracts; only a handful of contract detail URLs surfaced (e.g. /zmluva/8907711 'Zmluva o akceptácii platobných kariet', /zmluva/12680586 electronic banking services).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Discovery must be done inside CRZ's own search or over the bulk export, not via search engines; otherwise coverage will be badly biased.

negative_findings.description: OtvorenéZmluvy.sk (TIS / Aliancia Fair-play) is described in secondary sources but I did not reach a live working portal at a confirmed URL during this pass; only the TIS announcement page and a science-media article about the project were found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Project documented; current live endpoint unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Its enumerated list of ~130 non-CRZ registers would be the fastest way to close the municipal/long-tail coverage gap — worth a dedicated follow-up including web-archive lookup.

negative_findings.description: Searches combining 'prípravné trhové konzultácie' with 'platobné karty', 'platobný styk' and 'bankové služby' returned PTK index pages (NBS, MIRRI, UVO methodology) but no currently open payment/card-specific market consultation from the cell's buyers.
negative_findings.result_summary: PTK infrastructure exists and is well documented, but no live payments-topic PTK was visible at search time; the one confirmed payments-adjacent PTK (Štátna pokladnica, payment-system infrastructure modernisation) is marked completed with a March 2023 registration deadline.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms PTKs are a real early-warning channel for this cell but that they are episodic — monitoring must be continuous rather than point-in-time.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Slovenská pošta procurement page for payment terminals or cash-in-transit (preprava hotovosti) was found; posta.sk stated no commercial public tenders were currently announced.
negative_findings.result_summary: Payment-hardware demand from the postal operator is not exposed as a standing page; it surfaces only as individual tenders on the ERANET board or in the ÚVO bulletin.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection for this buyer must be event-driven on ERANET/ÚVO rather than page-driven.

negative_findings.description: ÚVO profile detail URLs appear in two path forms (/vyhladavanie/vyhladavanie-profilov/detail/<id> and /vyhladavanie-profilov/detail/<id>), some with legacy cHash query parameters, indicating a portal migration.
negative_findings.result_summary: URL scheme instability observed across search results; not fetched, so liveness of either form is unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any buyer-profile watchlist keyed on hard-coded ÚVO URLs risks silent breakage; resolve IDs through the profile search or open data instead.

negative_findings.description: The mfsr.sk procurement profile page fetched as navigation skeleton only — the substantive listing did not render for the fetcher.
negative_findings.result_summary: Page is live but content likely loaded dynamically or behind a sub-path; recorded as unverified rather than dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Static HTML scraping may return empty results for MF SR; a headless renderer is probably required.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Slovak for a national aggregator of municipal official noticeboards (úradná tabuľa) carrying výzvy na predkladanie ponúk. No single national electronic úradná tabuľa for all obce/mestá was found; disclosure is fragmented across each municipality's own CMS plus CRZ, EKS and the various commercial e-procurement platforms.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only per-municipality and per-VÚC noticeboards were identified (bratislava.sk, zilina.sk, nitra.sk, kosickazupa.sk, kosice-city.sk).
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Low-value contracts — the fastest-moving payments-acceptance segment — cannot be caught by one feed; the collector needs an enumerated per-entity watchlist of several hundred endpoints.

negative_findings.description: The DPMK / Mikroelektronika contract for 1,331 in-vehicle contactless readers (~EUR 1,492,064 incl. VAT) was reported in Slovak media/search summaries, but no primary ÚVO notice or CRZ contract URL for it was located within this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: Deal is attested only at second hand; the primary award document remains to be resolved.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Illustrates that award-level facts must be re-sourced to CRZ/ÚVO before use; media summaries alone are not citable evidence.

negative_findings.description: The ÚVO/NASES open-data publication of the procurement bulletin is documented, but the current concrete dataset/API URL could not be pinned down — historical references point to open.slovensko.sk and data.gov.sk, both of which have since migrated to data.slovensko.sk.
negative_findings.result_summary: Capability confirmed, endpoint unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Bulk XML ingestion would be far cheaper than scraping; a short follow-up to locate the live dataset would materially improve collection economics.

negative_findings.description: One search result rendered the uvo.gov.sk root as 'Error'. No conclusion is drawn: this is recorded as unverified, most likely transient or bot-defended, not as a dead source.
negative_findings.result_summary: Status unknown; deep links to uvo.gov.sk subpages resolved normally in results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: ÚVO is the backbone source for this cell; a false 'dead' verdict would gut the collection plan.

negative_findings.description: Could not resolve the ÚVO profile detail IDs for EXIMBANKA SR and Slovak Investment Holding in this pass. NBS (8643) and SZRB (9586) were resolved; the ÚVO profile search is a JavaScript SPA that did not yield the other two IDs through search-engine results.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two of four target authorities lack a stable ÚVO profile ID.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Without profile IDs the monitoring pipeline must fall back on name-string matching, which is fragile across diacritics and legal-name variants (EXIMBANKA SR / Exportno-importná banka Slovenskej republiky).

negative_findings.description: The e-procurement platform used by SZRB, Eximbanka and SIH was not established. NBS is confirmed on IS JOSEPHINE; szrb.sk names no platform and points only to its ÚVO profile, and one eTrhovisko (ezakazky.sk) item page appeared in an SZRB-context search without confirmation of the link.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only 1 of 4 authorities has a confirmed tendering platform.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Tender documentation, deadlines and supplier Q&A live on the platform, not in the notice; not knowing the platform means only shallow notice-level coverage for three of four banks.

negative_findings.description: An English-language search for NBS notices on TED returned only generic TED documentation and commercial TED-reseller pages, no actual notice URLs. TED's own search is a JS application not indexed usefully by web search.
negative_findings.result_summary: TED coverage asserted structurally (SIH confirms EU OJ publication) but no specific notice URL captured.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: TED is the best structured/API channel for this cell; it must be exercised through its API rather than via web search, and that has not been validated here.

negative_findings.description: NBS holds an exemption from the Centrálny register zmlúv and publishes contracts/orders/invoices only on nbs.sk under Act 546/2010, whereas SZRB, Eximbanka and SIH appear in CRZ.
negative_findings.result_summary: No single register covers all four authorities' contracts.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A CRZ-only pipeline would silently miss the single most interesting buyer in the cell (the central bank). Two separate collectors are required.

negative_findings.description: The English string 'Exim Bank' is heavily polluted: searches return Exim Bank Tanzania, Uganda, Bangladesh and Exim Bank Group. Similarly 'NBS' collides with UK/Serbian building societies and 'SIH' is a common acronym.
negative_findings.result_summary: English-only querying on these actor names is unreliable.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the mandatory-local-language rule for this cell: queries must use 'EXIMBANKA SR', 'Exportno-importná banka Slovenskej republiky', 'Národná banka Slovenska', 'Slovenská záručná a rozvojová banka' and IČO numbers, not English acronyms.

negative_findings.description: Both NBS and Eximbanka run parallel URL schemes: nbs.sk/o-narodnej-banke/verejne-obstaravanie/... alongside legacy www.nbs.sk/sk/verejne-obstaravanie/...; eximbanka.sk serves both a query-string CMS (?page_id=) and WordPress /wp-content/ PDFs.
negative_findings.result_summary: Duplicate/legacy URL trees observed on two of four target sites.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collectors keyed on one tree may quietly go stale or double-count; canonicalisation rules are needed, and old bookmarks should not be assumed dead on a single 404.

negative_findings.description: Despite Slovak-language searching with the exact idiomatic phrases ('pre dodávateľov', 'výberové konanie dodávateľ', 'kódex dodávateľov', 'nákup a obstarávanie'), no dedicated public supplier/vendor page was located for Slovenská sporiteľňa, Tatra banka, ČSOB Slovensko, 365.bank/Poštová banka, Prima banka, UniCredit Bank CZ&SK, PSS or mBank SK.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only VÚB banka has a confirmed public procurement page (/ludia/nakup-obstaravanie.html). All other SK banks returned merchant-side, product or unrelated results.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms the cell's core premise: for eight of nine target banks there is no direct, crawlable sourcing channel, so the bypass route must lean on group portals, e-sourcing platforms, and indirect registries rather than bank websites.

negative_findings.description: The Slovak/English term 'portál' + 'dodávateľ'/'supplier' for Tatra banka is dominated by MERCHANT acquiring products: 'Obchodnícky portál TB', 'Portál na splátky TB', 'Merchant portal'. Similar noise appears for other banks where 'dodávateľ' refers to the customer's own suppliers (e.g. VÚB fraud-warning page 'Pozor na falošných dodávateľov').
negative_findings.result_summary: Supplier-portal queries return acquiring/merchant product pages, not procurement.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any automated keyword sweep must exclude 'obchodník', 'merchant', 'akceptácia kariet', 'splátky' and fraud-advisory pages, or precision collapses.

negative_findings.description: https://www.vub.sk/ludia/nakup-obstaravanie.html returned HTTP 403 Forbidden to a plain automated fetch, while search-engine snippets confirm substantive procurement content on the page.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bot defence on vub.sk; content exists and is public in a browser. NOT recorded as dead.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most valuable direct source in this cell requires a browser-grade collector; a naive HTTP pipeline would wrongly mark the cell's best source as unavailable.

negative_findings.description: No public supplier-registration URL was found for Erste Group Procurement, Raiffeisen Bank International, KBC or UniCredit despite English, German and Italian searching. Only Intesa Sanpaolo's Portale Fornitori has a confirmed public self-registration endpoint.
negative_findings.result_summary: 1 of 5 relevant banking groups exposes a publicly addressable supplier portal.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: For Erste/RBI/KBC/UniCredit the sourcing channel is likely invitation-only or behind an unadvertised Ariba/Coupa tenant, meaning tender visibility for SLSP, Tatra banka, ČSOB and UniCredit SK must come from indirect signals (contracts, references, personnel, vendor press releases), not portals.

negative_findings.description: For mBank Slovensko no Slovak-language procurement or supplier vocabulary surfaced at all; the entity operates as a branch of Polish mBank S.A. and any sourcing terminology would be Polish ('dostawcy', 'zakupy', 'przetarg'), which was not searched in this run.
negative_findings.result_summary: mBank SK supplier channel unmapped; no sk-language footprint.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Language coverage for this actor is incomplete and must be closed with Polish-language search before mBank can be called a dead end.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated public supplier/tender portal was located for the large private retail banks in SK (Slovenská sporiteľňa, Tatra banka, ČSOB) using sk-language queries for 'portál pre dodávateľov', 'nákup', 'obstarávanie'.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only VÚB surfaced a 'Nákup a obstarávanie' page (and that returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch). Group-level tools (e.g. Erste/RBI/KBC central e-sourcing) were not identifiable from SK-domain search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The largest private banking buyers in Slovakia may source entirely through parent-group platforms, meaning their competitions are invisible to any SK platform scrape and require a different discovery route (group procurement sites, vendor-side references, contract registers).

negative_findings.description: 'Portál VO' / 'portalvo.sk' from the cell definition did not resolve to a distinct live commercial platform.
negative_findings.result_summary: Explicit domain-quoted search returned no such portal; nearest matches were ÚVO's own pages, voko.sk and obstaravania.egov.sk.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell brief may carry a stale or mis-remembered platform name; downstream verification should not spend budget chasing it, and voko.sk/egov.sk should be treated as the likely intended referents.

negative_findings.description: No SK-hosted instance of international corporate e-sourcing suites (SAP Ariba, Coupa, Jaggaer, GEP) serving Slovak banks was found within this cell's searches.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for private-sector bank sourcing surfaced only domestic platforms plus generic definitions of e-aukcia/tender.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If SK bank sourcing runs on Ariba-type suites, tender visibility depends on Ariba Discovery-style public postings — a whole source family currently uncovered.

negative_findings.description: ERANET client instances mostly gate their tender lists behind supplier registration.
negative_findings.result_summary: Instance URLs found repeatedly land on views/registration.html rather than an open list.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collection from ERANET instances may require registered accounts, changing the legal/ops profile of that route versus JOSEPHINE's open list.

negative_findings.description: Slovak-language searches for ATM servicing and cash-in-transit tenders (verejné obstarávanie servis bankomatov, preprava a spracovanie hotovosti) returned vendor marketing pages and generic procurement portals, but no individual ATM/CIT tender or award notice surfaced in general web results.
negative_findings.result_summary: General search engines do not index the deep contents of the ÚVO Vestník, EKS, JOSEPHINE or ERANET well enough to find individual payments-infrastructure notices; the notices must be reached by querying those systems directly with CPV and keyword filters.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that a search-engine-only collection strategy would produce near-zero coverage for this cell; budget must go to in-portal querying and API access instead.

negative_findings.description: The largest ATM fleets, POS estates and card-personalisation volumes in Slovakia sit with private commercial banks (Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB, Tatra banka, ČSOB) and acquirers (Global Payments Slovakia, Worldline, SKPAY), none of which are contracting authorities publishing in the Vestník.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches for POS terminal supply and card personalisation returned only commercial product pages, not tenders. No public tender channel was found for these buyers.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The commercially most valuable payments-infrastructure demand in SK is structurally invisible to A2 procurement monitoring; it must be tracked via a different workstream (vendor announcements, references, corporate registry, RFP rumours).

negative_findings.description: The seed query on payment gateway / instant payment integration contracts (zákazka platobná brána integrácia okamžité platby SEPA) yielded regulatory and association material (NBS, SBA) but no procurement notices and no settled Slovak tender wording for gateway integration.
negative_findings.result_summary: Found the regulatory driver and its deadlines, not the procurement artefacts.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The glossary for gateway/instant-payment procurement in SK is unproven; keyword crawlers built on guessed terms (platobná brána, integrácia okamžitých platieb) risk silent misses until validated against real notice text.

negative_findings.description: One search result for the ÚVO root domain was titled 'Error', suggesting the portal intermittently serves error pages.
negative_findings.result_summary: Treated as an unverified hypothesis, not evidence the portal is down. No fetch was performed to confirm.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A collector must tolerate transient failures on the single most important source rather than marking it dead; retry-with-backoff and alerting on sustained failure are required.

negative_findings.description: No Slovak independent ATM deployer (e.g. Euronet-type IAD) procurement or tender channel was identified within this cell's searches.
negative_findings.result_summary: Not searched to exhaustion; no evidence found either way.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Independent ATM deployers are a distinct buyer class for ATM hardware and CIT services; their absence from the map is a known blind spot rather than a confirmed absence.

negative_findings.description: No NCR Atleos Slovak-market press release, country page or bank reference was found in either sk or en searching.
negative_findings.result_summary: Searches returned only global ATM-industry comparisons and corporate spin-off coverage; no Slovakia-specific NCR Atleos disclosure surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: NCR/Atleos hardware is widely deployed in Slovakia (largely via Printec as channel partner), so the deal disclosure likely sits with the local partner rather than the OEM — collection should target partners, not Atleos PR.

negative_findings.description: No Thales/Gemalto press release or reference naming a Slovak bank card-issuance customer was found.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only generic global product pages (EMV cards, D1 issuing platform) returned; no SK-specific customer disclosure.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Card personalisation/issuance supply to Slovak banks remains undisclosed on the vendor side; this relationship will have to be inferred from bank card-back branding, NBS registers or tender records instead.

negative_findings.description: No Nexi Group press release specific to Slovakia or a Slovak bank was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Nexi PR archive exists and is crawlable, but keyword searching produced no Slovakia hit.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests Nexi has no publicly announced Slovak bank acquiring partnership to date; the archive is still worth monitoring rather than treating as covered.

negative_findings.description: Asseco CE reference page returned HTTP 403 to a plain fetch.
negative_findings.result_summary: https://ce.asseco.com/referencie/ → 403 Forbidden; the same domain is well indexed and other paths appear in search results, so this is presumed bot-defence rather than a dead page. Recorded as unverified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The single most valuable reference list in this cell needs a browser-grade fetcher; a naive crawler would wrongly mark it dead.

negative_findings.description: Slovak banks systematically do not name their IT suppliers, and vendors often anonymise bank clients in case studies ('banka', 'bankový sektor').
negative_findings.result_summary: Documented by a Forbes SK / Asseco-clipped article; corroborated by DATALAN case studies referring to unnamed 'banka'.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Vendor disclosure in SK is partially anonymised, so this cell's output frequently yields scope-without-buyer and must be triangulated against tender/award records from other cells.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated Slovak-language press room was found for Global Payments SK, Printec Slovakia, Euronet SK or Loomis SK.
negative_findings.result_summary: These local entities publish product/document pages but no discoverable SK press-release feed; announcements appear on group-level EN sites or via SK media wires.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must poll group-level EN press rooms plus SK media wires (SITA, TOUCHIT BrandIT) rather than expecting local vendor press feeds.

coverage_gaps.description: The exact CPV filter syntax and URL parameters of the ÚVO 'Vyhľadávanie zákaziek' interface and the EVO OrderSearch were not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Drive both search UIs in a browser session, capture the resulting query URLs/POST bodies, and codify them as reusable collector endpoints.

coverage_gaps.description: No contracting-authority shortlist yet for banking/payments demand (which SK public bodies actually buy acquiring, card issuing, cash logistics, ATM services, core-banking IT).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an actor map from CRZ/UVOstat supplier-side queries on the major SK banks and payment vendors (SLSP, VÚB, Tatra banka, ČSOB, Poštová banka, Prima banka, 365.bank, Global Payments, Worldline, Nexi, Diebold Nixdorf, NCR/Atleos, Loomis, Brink's, Printec) and invert to their public-sector counterparties.

coverage_gaps.description: ÚVO review/appeal decisions (rozhodnutia, námietky, revízne postupy) were not located as a distinct browsable source in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate the ÚVO decisions register / rozhodnutia section and assess it as a source — challenged banking/payments tenders yield unusually rich detail on requirements, pricing and competitor positioning.

coverage_gaps.description: Cell was scoped to the public/statutory channel; utilities-sector obstarávatelia and state-owned enterprises procuring payment acceptance (transport operators, Slovenská pošta, energy utilities) were not specifically probed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on obstarávateľ (utilities) notices and SOE buyer profiles for ticketing/payment-acceptance contracts.

coverage_gaps.description: English coverage of this cell is thin and mostly low-quality commercial tender-lead sites.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Rely on TED's English-language rendering of SK notices for EN-language reporting rather than commercial aggregators; avoid globaltenders/tendersinfo-class sites as sources.

coverage_gaps.description: The actual number and character of Slovak banking/payment notices on TED is unknown — no counts by CPV, year, buyer type or winner were established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a TED Search API expert query for country SVK across CPV 66xxxxxx (financial/banking/insurance), 30162000/30123000 (POS/card terminals) and 72xxxxxx banking-IT codes for the last 5 years, and record counts before designing the ongoing feed.

coverage_gaps.description: No agreed CPV code list for 'banking and payments' has been fixed for this run; scouting used ad-hoc codes (66110000, 66172000, 72212442).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define and version a canonical CPV allow-list (banking, payment processing, cash handling and transport, card personalisation, POS/ATM hardware, core-banking software, AML/KYC services) and store it alongside the collector config.

coverage_gaps.description: Notices published under the utilities/defence directives and under concessions use different eForms notice subtypes; these were not examined and may carry payment/cash-handling contracts of Slovak state entities.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate eForms notice subtypes in the SDK and confirm the collector's query does not silently exclude utilities, concessions or design contests.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell covers Slovak buyers, but Slovak/CEE payment vendors also win contracts published by buyers in other member states; those notices would be missed by a buyer-country=SVK filter.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a second TED query dimension filtering on winner/economic-operator country = SK, and on named vendor strings, independent of buyer country.

coverage_gaps.description: TED only carries above-threshold contracts; a large share of Slovak banking/payment procurement (especially municipal and small-agency card/POS/cash services) will sit below EU thresholds.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Explicitly pair the TED feed with the ÚVO Vestník feed owned by the national cell, and quantify the split once both feeds run.

coverage_gaps.description: Reuse conditions were not confirmed for ECEPP, the F&T Portal and opentender.eu; only TED/data.europa.eu are clearly open-reuse.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Check robots.txt and terms of use for each non-TED source and record an explicit collection_allowed verdict before automating.

coverage_gaps.description: EU-funded Slovak projects (Recovery and Resilience Plan, Partnership Agreement 2021-2027) generate procurement announced through national EU-funds portals rather than TED when below threshold; these were not scouted here.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assign a follow-up cell to Slovak EU-funds portals (e.g. partnerskadohoda.gov.sk, planobnovy.sk) as the funding-side counterpart to this EU publication layer.

coverage_gaps.description: EU-level oversight actors touching SK procurement — OLAF, EPPO (Slovakia participates), European Court of Auditors, and the CJEU/General Court on SK infringement cases — were not searched in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on OLAF/EPPO press releases mentioning Slovensko + verejné obstarávanie, ECA special reports on SK cohesion spending, and CURIA for SK procurement preliminary rulings.

coverage_gaps.description: Domestic financial-control actors other than NKÚ — Ministerstvo financií SR (Sekcia auditu a kontroly / vládny audit), Úrad vládneho auditu, and managing authorities' irregularity findings on EU-funded contracts — are unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search 'Úrad vládneho auditu správa', 'vládny audit verejné obstarávanie', 'nezrovnalosť riadiaci orgán korekcia' and map their publication registers.

coverage_gaps.description: Criminal-side oversight (Generálna prokuratúra SR, NAKA / Úrad boja proti korupcii, Špecializovaný trestný súd) which prosecutes procurement manipulation was not covered.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Map prosecution/court publication practice for procurement corruption cases; note that indictments often name contract values and intermediaries.

coverage_gaps.description: No machine-readable API or bulk export was confirmed for ÚVO decisions, PMÚ decisions, or NKÚ reports; NKÚ's list uses Liferay portlet pagination and ÚVO decisions are PDFs on fileadmin paths.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe for open-data endpoints on data.slovensko.sk for these publishers; otherwise budget for PDF-harvest + OCR/text-extraction pipeline with stable document-ID capture.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin: ÚVO, NKÚ and PMÚ publish substantive decisions almost exclusively in Slovak; only EU-level pages provide EN framing.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan for SK-language full-text search and machine translation in the pipeline; do not rely on EN queries to discover cases.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical depth of the ÚVO decision registers (how far back the online listings reach, and what moved to /dohlad/archiv) was not established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate https://www.uvo.gov.sk/dohlad/archiv and the fileadmin/dokumenty/rozhodnutia_* directories to determine earliest available year before designing the backfill.

coverage_gaps.description: No CPV code shortlist for banking and payments has been fixed. uvostat.sk exposes per-CPV pages (e.g. /cpvkod/{id}) and TenderRadar filters by CPV, but the specific CPV branches covering financial services, banking software, payment terminals/POS, ATMs, card issuance and related IT services were not enumerated in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Derive an explicit CPV shortlist from the EU CPV taxonomy (66xxxxxx financial/insurance, 48xxxxxx software, 30xxxxxx office/computing incl. payment terminals, 72xxxxxx IT services) and validate each against uvostat.sk CPV pages for actual Slovak notice volume.

coverage_gaps.description: The e-procurement execution platforms named by aggregators — EKS (Elektronický kontraktačný systém, elektronické trhovisko), JOSEPHINE, ERANET — were identified only indirectly, through third-party aggregators. Their own open-data/API surfaces were not investigated in this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Assign a follow-up pass to EKS (eks.sk / elektronickatrhovisko), JOSEPHINE and ERANET to determine whether each publishes open data or an API; low-value purchases (where much payments hardware and small IT is bought) live disproportionately on these platforms.

coverage_gaps.description: No archival/snapshot strategy was identified for notices that are delisted from the official portal, nor for defunct civil-society mirrors (znasichdani.sk). Web-archive coverage of Slovak procurement sites was not assessed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test Wayback Machine and Common Crawl coverage for uvo.gov.sk, znasichdani.sk and otvorenezmluvy.sk; adopt the OCDS all-time release plus Opentender bulk as the durable historical base layer.

coverage_gaps.description: Joining suppliers across ÚVO notices, CRZ contracts, OCDS records and company registers relies on IČO and on OCDS ocid, but no mapping between the identifier schemes used by uvostat.sk, Ekosystém.Slovensko.Digital and the OCDS publication was established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and test an identifier crosswalk early (IČO <-> uvostat obstarávateľ/dodávateľ id <-> ocid <-> TED notice id) before any volume collection; the Ekosystém RPO v2 dataset is the natural spine.

coverage_gaps.description: Re-use terms were not read in full for the commercial/semi-commercial analytics layers (uvostat.sk, transparex.sk, transpera.sk, tendermonitor.sk, tenderradar.sk) or for the Slovensko.Digital premium tier.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Before any automated collection from these hosts, read robots.txt and terms of use, and prefer licensed API access; restrict free-tier use to manual verification.

coverage_gaps.description: Municipal and self-government contract registers outside CRZ (the ~130 smaller registers that OtvorenéZmluvy aggregated, plus commercial register services such as eGovZmluvy/zmluvy.egov.sk) were touched only in passing.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Map the sub-CRZ registers used by municipalities, schools and regional authorities; relevant because local-government payment/POS and banking-services contracts often never reach CRZ or the ÚVO bulletin.

coverage_gaps.description: Member rosters of SBA, Slovenská FinTech asociácia, FINAS, ITAS and RÚZ were identified by URL but not individually fetched and parsed in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fetch and parse each members page, normalise names to legal entity + IČO via ORSR/RPO, and store as the A2 actor master list.

coverage_gaps.description: Payment/e-money providers passported into Slovakia from other Member States will not appear in SK-only registers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull EBA EUCLID PIR/CIR with host-country=SK and merge with the NBS PSD2 JSON.

coverage_gaps.description: This cell concentrated on supplier/actor registers; the contracting-authority side (ÚVO Register verejných obstarávateľov, state IT bodies, municipalities, Štátna pokladnica) was only touched via one URL.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Dedicate a follow-up pass to enumerating financial-sector-relevant contracting authorities and their ÚVO profiles.

coverage_gaps.description: No searches were run for stavebné sporiteľne, credit unions, crypto/VASP registers, or the Slovak Association of Insurance Companies, each of which may carry its own membership or licence list touching payments.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run local-language queries for 'stavebné sporiteľne zoznam', 'register poskytovateľov služieb virtuálnych mien', 'Slovenská asociácia poisťovní členovia'.

coverage_gaps.description: Regional/secondary outlets and aggregators not yet assessed: SME/Index SME, Pravda ekonomika, Euractiv.sk, TASR/teraz.sk, PC Revue/Nextech, Startitup, Zastavme korupciu.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a second pass with site-scoped SK queries (site:index.sme.sk, site:teraz.sk) on tender+banka keyword sets and profile each.

coverage_gaps.description: No systematic mapping yet of the named journalists and procurement lawyers who repeatedly break SK bank/state IT tender stories, nor of their personal blogs/LinkedIn/X accounts.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a byline-level actor map from Živé.sk, Denník E and Red Flags contributors; add their personal feeds as low-latency sources.

coverage_gaps.description: No decision recorded on subscribing to the paywalled titles that carry the highest-value content.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Cost/benefit review of Denník N+E, Trend and HN subscriptions for the collection programme.

coverage_gaps.description: Commercial-bank procurement (non-public) has no journalistic watchdog equivalent to Red Flags.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Compensate with vendor press rooms, bank annual reports, and IT integrator case studies as a separate cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Prípravné trhové konzultácie (statutory pre-tender market consultations under the Slovak public procurement act) were not searched; these are published by contracting authorities and are the most explicit legal pre-announcement of a tender.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on 'prípravné trhové konzultácie' across uvo.gov.sk, institutional websites and the electronic procurement platform, and treat it as a direct pre-tender source.

coverage_gaps.description: State-sector payment-heavy institutions were not individually profiled: Štátna pokladnica, Sociálna poisťovňa, Slovenská pošta, VšZP, DataCentrum MF SR, NASES, Úrad vlády, self-governing regions and Bratislava/Košice city IT units.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an actor map with each institution's news feed, career page, budget documents and MetaIS records; these are the buyers whose weak signals matter most for payments.

coverage_gaps.description: Government legislative and cabinet pipelines (rokovania.gov.sk cabinet materials, slov-lex legislative process) were not covered; strategy documents and system mandates are approved there before any budget or tender exists.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add rokovania.gov.sk and slov-lex.sk keyword monitoring for payment/e-government system names.

coverage_gaps.description: Bank-side strategy artefacts (annual reports, Pillar 3 disclosures, parent-group technology plans for Erste/Intesa/RBI/KBC) that name planned payment platform investments were not covered by this cell's pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add issuer/parent-group investor materials as an indirect pre-procurement signal for commercial-bank technology spend.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage in this cell was thin — most productive material is Slovak-only. EU-level sources (EU Recovery and Resilience Scoreboard country page, Digital Europe Programme work programmes) were only touched indirectly.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run an EN pass on the EC RRF scoreboard for Slovakia and Digital Europe/CEF work programmes to capture the EU-side view of the same pipeline.

coverage_gaps.description: Regional self-government (VÚC / samosprávne kraje) and the large state-owned enterprises outside those checked (ŽSR, ZSSK, Slovenská elektrizačná prenosová sústava, vodárenské spoločnosti, VšZP) were not individually scouted, yet each is a significant buyer of card acceptance, cash handling and account services.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate all 8 VÚCs and the top ~20 state-owned enterprises, resolve each to its CRZ entity page and its own zmluvy/objednávky/faktúry page, and add them as templated sources.

coverage_gaps.description: No supplier-side index was established mapping SK bank / PSP legal entities (IČO) to their public contracts — the analysis-critical join. Slovenská sporiteľňa, VÚB, Tatra banka, ČSOB, Prima banka, Poštová banka, 365.bank, UniCredit, plus acquirers and terminal vendors were not enumerated with IČOs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build an IČO reference list of SK banks, payment institutions, acquirers and terminal/ATM vendors (from NBS register of supervised entities and RPO), then drive all CRZ/invoice harvesting by IČO rather than free text.

coverage_gaps.description: Glossary coverage was built for contract/invoice terminology (zmluva, objednávka, faktúra, dodávateľ, akceptácia platobných kariet, platobná brána, bankomat, hotovostné operácie, ceniny) but not validated against actual CRZ contract-title conventions; Hungarian-minority and English-in-Slovak variants were not tested.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Derive the real title vocabulary empirically by frequency-analysing contract titles in the bulk XML export for banking/payment suppliers, then feed the top n-grams back as search terms.

coverage_gaps.description: CRZ starts 1.1.2011 and the eGovZmluvy-to-CRZ auto-forwarding only began 1.4.2022; pre-2022 municipal contracts may exist only on the originating platform or in municipal archives (e.g. archivzverejnovanie.bratislava.sk).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For any longitudinal claim before 2022, harvest the originating municipal/platform registers and archive sites separately rather than assuming CRZ completeness.

coverage_gaps.description: Reuse licence for the CRZ bulk export and for the third-party aggregators (Slovensko.Digital Datahub, uvostat, eGovZmluvy) was not confirmed, and Datahub is explicitly freemium with a price list.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Confirm the open-data licence on the national catalogue entry and read each aggregator's ToS before any commercial market-intelligence reuse or redistribution.

coverage_gaps.description: Private health insurers Dôvera and Union have no confirmed procurement profile pages yet; their buyer status is subject to a contested ÚVO ruling.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Re-run profile-registry lookups for IČO 35942436 (Dôvera) and 31322051 (Union) quarterly, and track the ÚVO/court outcome.

coverage_gaps.description: EKS (Elektronický kontraktačný systém) — the SK electronic marketplace used by Sociálna poisťovňa and others for below-threshold contracts — was referenced but not yet profiled as a source.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Profile eks.sk as a separate candidate source and test whether buyer-filtered listings/exports are available.

coverage_gaps.description: Buyer-to-platform mapping is only partially established: ERANET (Slovenská pošta), JOSEPHINE and eZakazky (ŽSR), IS EVO (Štátna pokladnica, Finančná správa). Platform of record for MF SR, Sociálna poisťovňa, VšZP and ZSSK not confirmed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: For each remaining buyer, fetch its procurement page and record the named e-procurement system, then add the buyer-scoped platform URL as a candidate.

coverage_gaps.description: ÚVO bulletin open data on data.gov.sk was referenced second-hand but the actual dataset endpoint was not located in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and profile the ÚVO/vestník dataset on data.gov.sk as a bulk, machine-readable backbone for buyer-keyed monitoring.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of these buyers' procurement is thin — only generic market guides and low-quality commercial tender aggregators surfaced.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Treat Slovak as the mandatory working language for this cell; use TED (EU) English notices only for above-threshold cross-checks.

coverage_gaps.description: Only a sample of municipal buyers was reached (Bratislava, Košice, Prešov, Žilina, Nitra, Humenné, Ružomberok). Slovakia has ~140 mestá, 2,700+ obce, 8 VÚC, 17+22 mestské časti and dozens of dopravné podniky / technické služby.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build the buyer universe programmatically from ÚVO buyer profiles filtered by legal form / SK NACE, then attach each entity's own noticeboard URL.

coverage_gaps.description: Cash-collection / cash-in-transit and cash-handling services procured by municipalities (prevoz cenín, spracovanie hotovosti, inkaso miestnych daní a poplatkov) were not directly searched; only ticketing and parking were probed in depth.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run dedicated sk queries: 'prevoz peňazí a cenín zákazka mesto', 'spracovanie hotovosti obstarávanie samospráva', 'inkaso miestnych poplatkov platobná brána mesto'.

coverage_gaps.description: ERANET and other smaller e-procurement platforms (11+ exist in SK) expose tenders on per-buyer subdomains that were not enumerated; the tail of platforms beyond Josephine/eZakazky/EKS/ERANET is unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Compile the full platform list (a 2020 practitioner inventory of '11 + 1 + X' systems exists) and map which municipal buyers use which.

coverage_gaps.description: Hungarian-language publication by southern Slovak municipalities (Komárno, Dunajská Streda, Rimavská Sobota) was not searched, although some bilingual noticeboards exist.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add hu-language probes ('közbeszerzés', 'ajánlattételi felhívás', 'parkolás bankkártyás fizetés') for the bilingual districts.

coverage_gaps.description: Archives of low-value contracts (e.g. the VUCKE §9(9) archive runs to at least page 17) were identified but not traversed, so no historical baseline of municipal payments spend was established.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Backfill the paginated low-value archives of all 8 VÚC and the largest cities for at least 5 years.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed tendering platform for SZRB, Eximbanka SR or SIH.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Open one recent notice for each authority from the Vestník or its ÚVO profile and read the 'komunikácia a výmena informácií' section, which names the platform (JOSEPHINE / IS EPVO-EVO / eZakazky / ERANET); record it in the actor map.

coverage_gaps.description: No API/open-data endpoint validated for ÚVO (ISEPVO/eForms), CRZ or TED in this pass; all findings rest on HTML.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test the ÚVO eForms/open-data exports, the CRZ open-data download, and the TED Search API with country=SK and buyer-name filters; prefer these over scraping the SPAs.

coverage_gaps.description: No CPV code list has been fixed for this cell's technology interests (banknote processing and sorting machines, security printing, ATM/cash equipment, core banking software, payment clearing systems).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build a CPV shortlist (e.g. 30160000 magnetic cards, 30132000, 48000000 software, 48100000, 66000000 financial services, 79800000 printing/security printing, 50000000 repair and maintenance) and use it as a standing filter across ÚVO and TED, independent of buyer name.

coverage_gaps.description: PTK (preliminary market consultation) coverage is confirmed only for NBS; it is unknown whether SZRB, Eximbanka or SIH publish PTKs at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search 'prípravné trhové konzultácie' plus each institution name and check the ÚVO PTK section; if absent, record it explicitly so the pipeline does not silently assume coverage.

coverage_gaps.description: Not covered: ÚVO revision/appeal decisions (rozhodnutia, námietky) and NKÚ SR audit reports on state financial institutions, both of which expose contested and cancelled tenders — often the most informative cases.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add ÚVO 'Rozhodnutia' / 'Register konečných užívateľov výhod' and NKÚ SR (nku.gov.sk) report search to a follow-up scouting pass for this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: NBS as a Eurosystem NCB may participate in ECB/Eurosystem joint procurement (e.g. banknote-related tenders published by the ECB), which would not surface in Slovak registers at all.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout the ECB procurement portal and Eurosystem joint-procurement notices in a separate pass and link them to NBS as participating NCB.

coverage_gaps.description: Polish-language search for mBank S.A. supplier/procurement channels ('dostawcy', 'zakupy', 'przetarg', 'portal dostawcy') was not performed; Czech-language search for ČSOB group procurement ('dodavatelé', 'nákup', 'výběrové řízení') was also not performed even though ČSOB SK sits under the CZ/KBC structure.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a follow-up pass in pl and cs against mbank.pl, csob.cz and kbc-group service-company domains.

coverage_gaps.description: No check was made of whether SK banks run sourcing through group IT/shared-service subsidiaries that DO publish tenders (e.g. Erste's service companies, KBC Global Services CZ, PB Servis / SKPAY in the 365.bank group, VÚB Generali, Tatra-Leasing).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate each bank's Slovak subsidiaries via ORSR/FinStat and repeat the supplier-page sweep at subsidiary level; several of these are more likely than the bank to publish a tender.

coverage_gaps.description: The Slovak commercial e-sourcing platforms (JOSEPHINE/PROEBIZ, ERANET, TENDERnet, evo.gov.sk, EVOSERVIS) were identified but not systematically queried for bank buyers; whether any of the nine target banks has a buyer profile there is untested.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a name/IČO sweep for all nine banks and their subsidiaries across the public listing pages of each Slovak e-sourcing platform; a single hit would convert an invisible channel into a monitorable feed.

coverage_gaps.description: Two high-yield indirect Slovak registries were not queried in this run: CRZ (Centrálny register zmlúv, crz.gov.sk) and RPVS (Register partnerov verejného sektora, rpvs.gov.sk). Banks and their vendors appear in both, and RPVS discloses beneficial owners of any company contracting with the state.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add crz.gov.sk and rpvs.gov.sk sweeps keyed on bank IČOs and on known banking-technology vendors as a standing indirect feed.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor-side disclosure was not scouted: technology suppliers routinely publish reference/case-study announcements naming the SK bank that awarded them work, which is often the ONLY public trace of a private-bank RFP outcome.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a vendor-press-release and reference-page watchlist (core banking, ATM/self-service, card processing, cash handling, IT integrators active in SK) as a complementary indirect route.

coverage_gaps.description: Private commercial banks and payment institutions as buyers are represented almost entirely by inference; only VÚB and NBS were pinned to concrete procurement pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass per institution (SLSP, Tatra banka, ČSOB, UniCredit SK, Prima banka, 365.bank, Poštová banka, Diners/payment acquirers) on '<bank> dodávatelia / nákup / obstarávanie / general terms for suppliers', plus parent-group procurement portals.

coverage_gaps.description: Per-client subdomain instances of ERANET and PROEBIZ were sampled, not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically enumerate *.eranet.sk and *.proebiz.com (footer links, certificate transparency logs, passive DNS) to build a complete buyer-instance registry.

coverage_gaps.description: ToS / robots.txt and paid-tier licensing terms of the monitoring services (Transpera, TenderRadar, Tender Monitor, ADVAL, tender.sk) were not reviewed.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Before any automated ingestion, review each service's ToS and prefer licensed feeds/email alerts over scraping.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is thin because the platforms are overwhelmingly Slovak-only; only generic EN queries were productive.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Use EN chiefly for vendor/group-level sourcing suites and for cross-border (CZ/PL) JOSEPHINE coverage; keep primary discovery in SK.

coverage_gaps.description: Independent ATM deployers and non-bank cash operators (IAD model) in Slovakia were not mapped: no operator list, no procurement or supplier channel identified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on SK independent ATM deployers (search: nezávislý prevádzkovateľ bankomatov, bankomatová sieť, výber hotovosti bez banky) and cross-check NBS registers of payment service providers.

coverage_gaps.description: CPV codes proposed for filtering (30123600 ATMs, 30162000 smart cards, 79710000 security services, 50000000 maintenance) were inferred, not confirmed against actual Slovak notices for ATM/CIT/terminal contracts.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pull a sample of 20-50 real SK notices from TED and the Vestník in these product areas and derive the CPV distribution empirically before locking the collector's filter set.

coverage_gaps.description: Commercial bank and acquirer procurement (the bulk of POS, card personalisation and ATM-estate spend) has no public tender channel, leaving A2 monitoring blind to the highest-value deals.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Escalate to a non-procurement workstream: track vendor press releases and case studies (Global Payments SK, Worldline SK, SKPAY), bank annual reports, and corporate-registry contract signals.

coverage_gaps.description: Zákazky s nízkou hodnotou (low-value contracts) — where most individual terminal, kiosk and servicing purchases sit — are dispersed across thousands of buyer websites and EKS, and are not comprehensively covered by any free source found.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Either subscribe to a commercial aggregator with low-value coverage (tender.sk claims 40,000+ sources) or accept documented under-coverage of this layer and state it in every derived metric.

coverage_gaps.description: ERANET is deployed as many per-buyer instances and only the Slovenská pošta instance was identified; the rest of the instance list is unmapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate ERANET (and similar) instances by crawling ÚVO buyer profiles for outbound e-procurement links, then register each relevant instance as its own source.

coverage_gaps.description: The most analysis-ready SK procurement dataset (UVOstat API) is token-gated with only /api/subjekty free; the rest is paid, and tender.sk is subscription-only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Decide early between paying for UVOstat API access and building an in-house Vestník/TED extractor; consult the Slovensko.Digital 'dáta vestníka' thread for the current DIY route.

coverage_gaps.description: Ness (Ness Slovensko / Ness KDC Košice), Atos/Eviden SK, DXC, IBM SK, Accenture SK and Deutsche Telekom IT Solutions Slovakia were not individually crawled for banking reference pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a second pass over the ITAS member directory and each of these vendors' SK reference/case-study sections with the terms 'referencie', 'prípadové štúdie', 'bankovníctvo'.

coverage_gaps.description: Payments-specific SK vendors beyond the seed list (e.g. card personalisation bureaus, POS distributors, fintech processors serving Slovak banks) were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Snowball from NBS payment-institution registers and from Global Payments/Printec partner pages to build a payments-vendor actor list, then crawl each for references.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor LinkedIn pages, conference/sponsorship materials and job ads (which name bank projects) were not explored as disclosure channels.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a pass over vendor LinkedIn posts and SK job postings mentioning specific bank clients/technologies; assess ToS before automating.

coverage_gaps.description: No historical archive strategy tested for vendor reference pages that get pruned when contracts end.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair each vendor reference/press URL with Wayback Machine snapshots to recover removed client references and date contract lifecycles.

coverage_gaps.description: Vendor claims are promotional and often anonymised; no cross-check pathway to award records was defined within this cell.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Define a join between vendor-page evidence (client, scope, date) and public-procurement/award data collected by other cells, keyed on vendor IČO from FinStat/ORSR.

briefs: Slovak public procurement of banking and payments services is anchored on one statutory spine: ÚVO's Vestník verejného obstarávania (mandatory under zák. 343/2015 Z.z.), whose notices are published daily as open XML datasets on data.slovensko.sk and mirrored above-threshold to TED — together these three give near-complete, machine-readable coverage of contract and award notices with CPV 66xxx, 30144000/30233300 and 72xxx. The procedure layer sits in IS EVO / Elektronická platforma (evo.isepvo.sk), which carries the súťažné podklady where POS terminal, ATM and card-processing specifications actually live, while below-threshold and low-value purchases run through EKS/elektronické trhovisko and the resulting signed contracts surface in the Centrálny register zmlúv. A useful secondary tier of aggregators — UVOstat, Slovensko.Digital's APIs, OpenTender/OCDS and commercial monitors such as verejnesutaze.sk — makes historical and cross-country analysis far cheaper, but every figure should be re-verified against the ÚVO primary notice. The main practical constraint found is discovery, not access: individual notices are effectively invisible to web search, so collection must be built on the portals' own CPV search, the Vestník XML feed and the TED API.

The EU publication layer for Slovak banking and payments procurement is anchored on TED, which since November 2022 publishes Slovak above-threshold notices in the eForms standard and exposes them through an unauthenticated Search API, bulk XML packages and the TED Open Data Service — making it the best-structured and most machine-tractable channel in this run, and clearly superior to the national bulletin for automated collection. Slovak notices reach TED via the ÚVO eForms information system acting as eSender, so TED and the ÚVO Vestník are two renderings of the same underlying filings, with TED carrying only the above-threshold subset and the national bulletin carrying the below-threshold remainder. The EU Funding & Tenders Portal adds a distinct, smaller stream of EU-institution contracts and programme calls where Slovak financial-sector actors appear as bidders or beneficiaries. The IFI channel is thinner than the cell rationale assumed: EBRD notices for Slovakia now flow exclusively through ECEPP and the Slovak examples found are energy and transport, while EIB's Slovak book is energy, urban and SME credit lines intermediated by Eximbanka — so IFI sources are worth low-frequency monitoring mainly as leading indicators of which institutions are scaling programmes, not as a procurement feed.

Slovakia's procurement remedy and audit trail is concentrated in four institutions with well-defined but PDF-heavy public registers: ÚVO (objections, review of contracting authority acts, administrative-offence fines, inspections, the transitional Rada ÚVO appeal body, and the statutory debarment register), NKÚ SR as supreme audit institution (audit protocols, summary reports, and a forward-looking list of ongoing audits), PMÚ SR for bid-rigging/cartel decisions plus its transparency document portal, and the courts via Slov-Lex, justice.gov.sk and the commercial aggregator Judikáty.info for administrative review of ÚVO and PMÚ decisions. These channels are the main way banking and payments contract details — bid values, disqualifications, cancelled and re-run tenders — become visible after the fact, since award notices routinely omit them. The binding constraint is not availability but retrievability: none of the registers offers sector or CPV filtering, decisions are published as PDFs on legacy CMS paths, and no confirmed API or bulk export was found, so collection must be full-corpus harvest with in-house keyword classification against a Slovak banking/payments glossary. Aggregators (Uvostat, Judikáty.info) and watchdog output (Transparency International Slovensko) are useful discovery and redundancy layers but must always be resolved back to the primary decision document before anything is asserted.

Slovakia has an unusually deep open-data and analytics layer over public procurement, in three tiers: (1) official machine-readable publication — the national catalogue at data.slovensko.sk (with a DCAT-AP-SK SPARQL endpoint) carrying ÚVO Vestník datasets, the legacy CKAN portal data.gov.sk, and the CRZ contract register with predictable daily XML change-batch exports since 2011; (2) civil-society re-publication — Ekosystém.Slovensko.Digital's weekly SQL dumps and rate-limited APIs over CRZ and the company registers, Red Flags for state IT project scoring, Transparency International Slovensko's tooling and methodologies, and Nadácia Zastavme korupciu's quantitative analyses of the post-2024 collapse in competitive tendering; and (3) standardised/international mirrors — the Slovak OCDS publication in the OCP Data Registry, Opentender.eu (GTI/DIGIWHIST, which adds below-threshold national data to TED), plus TED Open Data and the EU Public Procurement Data Space. A commercial analytics tier (uvostat.sk, transparex.sk with its T-index, transpera.sk, tendermonitor.sk, tenderradar.sk) adds supplier/buyer profiling and CPV-level market metrics that the official portals cannot answer, at the cost of paywalls and restrictive terms. The main weaknesses of the cell are that the flagship beneficial-ownership tool znasichdani.sk is defunct (DNS failure plus reporting of a 2018 shutdown), no first-party ÚVO API was confirmed, and nothing in the ecosystem is sector-specific — banking and payments relevance must be carved out ourselves via a CPV shortlist and a curated buyer/supplier list.

Slovakia's actor universe for banking and payments is unusually well served by statutory registers: NBS publishes both a sector-browsable supervised-entity database and a machine-readable daily PSD2 JSON feed, while the Ministry of Justice's RPVS makes registration legally compulsory for anyone contracting with the state, and ÚVO maintains a pre-qualified list of economic operators. Together these four give a near-complete, join-ready supplier and licence-holder list keyed on IČO, with ORSR/RPO and registeruz.sk supplying identity and scale, and EBA EUCLID closing the cross-border passporting gap. The association layer is fragmented — one banking association (SBA, ~23 members covering >99% of the sector), one leasing association (ALS, ~32 members), two competing fintech bodies (Slovenská FinTech asociácia and FINAS) and ITAS for IT vendors — so no single roster covers the vendor side and several must be merged. The main outstanding work is mechanical: fetch and parse the individual membership pages and confirm bulk-access routes for ORSR/RPO, since no dedicated Slovak cards/payments trade association appears to exist to shortcut that vendor mapping.

Slovak media coverage of banking/payments procurement splits into three usable layers: paywalled business journalism (Trend, HN, Denník E, Forbes SK) that names winners and controversies; open IT trade press (Živé.sk, ITnews.sk, TOUCHIT, plus the specialist FinReport.sk) that carries technical detail and early weak signals, often PR-sourced; and a professional/watchdog layer (Slovensko.Digital Red Flags and its forum, Transparency International SK, epravo.sk, overejnomobstaravani.sk and law-firm blogs) that translates notices into assessments and acts as the best pointer set into ÚVO/CRZ records. Red Flags and Živé.sk are the highest-value nodes; the paywall on the business titles is the main structural constraint. The clearest blind spot is private commercial-bank procurement, which no Slovak outlet covers systematically and which will need vendor- and report-based sourcing instead.

Slovakia has an unusually rich set of legally mandated pre-tender artefacts: MIRRI publishes project documentation and feasibility studies for public comment, MF SR's Útvar hodnoty za peniaze must appraise IT investments above roughly EUR 10m before procurement starts, and MetaIS registers every state information system and project. Together with the Plán obnovy (Component 17) and Program Slovensko call pipelines, these name planned payment and e-government systems months to years before any award notice. Weak signals on the commercial-bank side are thinner: bank vendor days are not published, so job boards (profesia.sk, bank career pages) and third-party conference agendas — ITAPA above all, plus FinNext and NBS events — are the practical substitutes for reading which vendors and which institutions are converging. The highest-value next step is a dedicated pass on 'prípravné trhové konzultácie' and on the payment-heavy state buyers (Štátna pokladnica, Sociálna poisťovňa, Slovenská pošta, DataCentrum), which this cell did not profile.

Slovakia's signed-contract layer is unusually rich: because a mandatorily-published contract only takes effect the day after publication, the Centrálny register zmlúv (crz.gov.sk, with an institution-indexed mirror at zmluvy.gov.sk) holds the actual banking and payment contracts of the state — counterparty, price and PDF — including direct awards with no tender notice. The practical collection spine is the daily XML change-batch bulk export catalogued on the national open-data portal (migrated from data.gov.sk to data.slovensko.sk), since there is no official CRZ query API; commercial aggregators (Slovensko.Digital Datahub, uvostat) and open-source scrapers exist as accelerators. Below CRZ sits the institution-level layer that CRZ contract metadata misses: NBS (the one entity with a standing publication exemption, so its own zmluvy/objednávky/faktúry pages are the only channel), Štátna pokladnica with its account and payment-gateway terms, Sociálna poisťovňa, Finančná správa, Slovenská pošta, ministries and municipalities such as Bratislava, plus SaaS platforms (eGovZmluvy, RZOF) that carry the long tail. The main analytic caveat is legal: §5a ods. 5 of Act 211/2000 lets payment-services and financial-instrument contracts be disclosed as a bare notice of conclusion, so a missing contract must be treated as censored data, not as absence of a deal.

Slovak banking/payments demand from state buyers is fragmented across three layers: each buyer's own procurement page (which alone carries plans and prípravné trhové konzultácie, the earliest signal — Štátna pokladnica's payment-systems infrastructure consultation is the clearest confirmed example), the statutory ÚVO buyer profile that is the legal record, and a buyer-specific e-procurement platform (ERANET for Slovenská pošta, JOSEPHINE and eZakazky for ŽSR, IS EVO for treasury and tax administration) that carries below-threshold and commercial tenders never reaching the bulletin. The highest-value targets are Štátna pokladnica, Slovenská pošta and ZSSK, whose cash, counter and ticketing estates generate concrete payment-terminal and acceptance demand. Aggregators uvostat.sk and verejnesutaze.sk provide buyer-keyed historical dossiers that are far easier to query than the ÚVO portal, but should be treated as secondary. The main structural risks are ÚVO URL-scheme instability, JS-rendered pages (mfsr.sk, ERANET) defeating static scraping, and an unresolved regulatory question over whether Dôvera and Union become obliged buyers.

Slovak municipal and regional payments procurement is legally centralised but practically fragmented: above-threshold notices land in the ÚVO vestník and TED, signed contracts land in the Centrálny register zmlúv (mandatory for samosprávy since March 2022), and commodity purchases run through the state EKS marketplace — but the fastest-moving layer, zákazky s nízkou hodnotou for ticketing, e-parking and cash handling, is scattered across each buyer's own úradná tabuľa and across at least four commercial e-procurement platforms (JOSEPHINE ~22%, eZakazky ~8%, ERANET ~8%, plus a long tail). The highest-value buyers for this cell are the municipal transport companies (DPB, DPMK, DPMP, all now deploying in-vehicle contactless validators) and city parking schemes (PAAS Bratislava, Žilina, Ružomberok, Humenné), each of which also leaves traces on vendor reference pages and specialist portals such as imhd.sk. A workable collection design is therefore three-tier: bulk ingest ÚVO/TED/CRZ as the authoritative spine, poll an enumerated watchlist of a few hundred municipal, borough, VÚC and mestský-podnik noticeboards for the sub-threshold layer, and use aggregators (verejnesutaze.sk, uvostat.sk) and vendor announcements purely as pointers to be resolved back to primary records.

Slovakia's four state-owned/controlled financial institutions are all subject to Act 343/2015 Z.z., so their procurement is unusually legible: each maintains a profil verejného obstarávateľa both on its own site and on the ÚVO portal (NBS = profile 8643, SZRB = 9586; Eximbanka and SIH IDs still unresolved), with notices duplicated into the daily Vestník and, above threshold, into TED. The richest and earliest signal sits with NBS, which publishes preliminary market consultations (PTK) months before tendering and runs all above-threshold procedures in IS JOSEPHINE — where confirmed tenders include banknote-processing equipment servicing and supervision/regulation case systems. A key structural asymmetry: NBS is exempt from the Centrálny register zmlúv and discloses contracts, orders and invoices only on nbs.sk, while SZRB, Eximbanka and SIH appear in CRZ, so award-side collection needs two distinct paths. SIH is a different animal — it procures financial intermediaries rather than technology — and aggregators (uvostat.sk, sk.openprocurements.com, verejnesutaze.sk) plus SITA Financie serve as convenience indexes and narrative context, never as primary evidence.

Slovakia's systemic banks are private and outside ÚVO, and this scouting run confirms the consequence empirically: of the nine target banks, only VÚB publishes a genuine Slovak-language procurement page (vub.sk/ludia/nakup-obstaravanie.html, bot-defended with HTTP 403 to plain fetch), and only one of five parent groups - Intesa Sanpaolo - exposes a publicly addressable supplier portal with open self-registration. Erste Group Procurement, RBI, KBC and UniCredit are structurally identifiable as the real sourcing decision points for SLSP, Tatra banka, ČSOB SK and UniCredit SK, but none advertises a reachable registration endpoint, so their tender flow is effectively invitation-only.
